findings.issue: Cited n1292 (Nikkei Asia, 'Japan's trading houses raise outlooks on weak yen, non-resource businesses') carries the 2023-11-06 08:00 placeholder, so it may have been published up to 17:00 JST on 7 November. A Tokyo roundup of trading-house outlooks most plausibly followed results released in Japanese business hours on the edition date, after the 00:00 UTC cutoff. The completed-event claim is doubtful, and it was the only trading-house evidence in the edition.
findings.resolution: Stopped citing n1292. JP now cites n0516 (Reuters, Toyota rides weak yen and hybrid demand to blowout profit, 2023-11-01). Underowned theme 4 now cites n1154 (Asahi Shimbun, Toyota profits zoom on cheap yen, 2023-11-01) and is retitled 'Japan's weak-yen exporters'. The JP Playbook no longer names trading houses.

findings.issue: Cited n1528 (TSN, 'Ukraine has sent a note to Poland regarding the border blocking') is stamped 2023-11-01. The Polish hauliers' border blockade it refers to only began on 6 November, and no own-date headline shows a blockade in place on 1 November. The record is therefore likely misdated (a later vintage), so the diplomatic-note claim cannot be safely timed.
findings.resolution: Stopped citing n1528. Replaced the sentence with n1646 (Interia, 2023-11-02: will Russia resume nuclear tests after withdrawing from a key treaty).

findings.issue: n0023 (Real Estate, 2023-10-25, 'November interest rate hike all but guaranteed') is a preview of the RBA decision published 13 days before cutoff. That is outside the seven-day window for previews by meaning, although its 'mon' category passed the verifier.
findings.resolution: Replaced it with n0071 (The Guardian, 2023-11-05, if interest rates rise again it may be because inflation fears lost their anchor). n0078 and n0062 still support the convergence on a hike.

findings.issue: Index levels (S&P 500, VIX, DXY, Euro Stoxx 50, Hang Seng, Shanghai Composite, Nikkei 225, ASX 200) were quoted without a unit. The contract requires prices in currency or index points.
findings.resolution: Added 'index points' to each quoted index level.

findings.issue: 'The DXY eased 0.85% to 105.22' gave no horizon. The card's 1-session DXY move is +0.19%, and -0.85% is the 5-session move.
'Term-premium unwind after the Treasury said it would increase most auction sizes [[n0094]]' implied that larger auctions caused the yield fall. The headline supports only the size increase.
findings.resolution: Reworded to 'even though the Treasury said it would increase most auction sizes'.

findings.issue: 'Stan Druckenmiller told Fortune...' n0487 does not establish that he gave Fortune an interview.
findings.resolution: Changed to 'Fortune reported that Stan Druckenmiller is really nervous...'.

findings.issue: 'the strongest post-event story in our coverage' describes the edition's own coverage instead of the market.
findings.resolution: Changed to 'the strongest equity story among the six regions'. The PL Markets part supports this with EPOL +17.94% over 20 sessions on the card.

findings.issue: The text added 'as a regulated utility', which is not in headline n0623, and claimed without support that 'merchant players are keen to own' the assets Duke is selling.
findings.resolution: Reworded to stay within the headline and frame it as an incumbent narrowing its focus while firm power commands the premium.

findings.issue: Filler sentence: 'Mercedes-Benz published its third-quarter results [[n1064]]' added nothing.
findings.resolution: Replaced it with a card-based comparison of German automakers over 20 sessions: Mercedes -9.33%, BMW -1.92%, VOW3 -0.62%.

findings.issue: 'Supply constraints are easing' overstated n1211, which reports only that Lilly is planning expansions. The Yahoo source tag also sat after Mondelez, which is not a card instrument.
findings.resolution: Changed to 'should ease' and moved the source tag next to the PepsiCo and P&G figures.

findings.issue: The quoted phrase 'most significant' profit was attributed to Reuters ('what it called'). The quotation marks in the headline indicate it is the company's wording.
The text said CNBC reports US Mounjaro supply has improved. In the headline, Eli Lilly makes that statement.
findings.resolution: Reworded to say Lilly says supply has improved, according to CNBC.

scope_limits: Evidence was limited to the 2023-11-07 frozen feed (tools/digest.py, with exclusions applied), the 2023-11-07 card (tools/showcard.py) and exclusions/2023-11-07.json. No other date, data/, cache/ or web source was read.
Each claim was checked against its headline only, not against an imagined article body. Card numbers were checked for instrument, session, horizon and unit.

Every cited record stamped 2023-11-06 08:00 was assessed for whether the event it reports plausibly happened before 00:00 UTC. The following were kept as plausibly pre-cutoff: OpenAI DevDay items (keynote about 18:00 UTC on 6 Nov); Citi job cuts n0902/n0903; Disney CFO n0909/n1286; Dish results n1284; NRG n0938; Newmont n0940; WeWork halt n0973/n0974 (the halt only; no filing is claimed); Lyft preview n0944; Duda address n1714; RBA previews n0075/n0078 (published before the 03:30 UTC decision, used only as expectations); Bloomberg He Lifeng n0194, Nikkei Micron n1298 and JoongAng Samsung share sale n0949 (none is tied to an edition-date release). The exact minute of publication for these placeholders cannot be verified.
The RBA decision of 7 November and China trade data due on 7 November appear only as pending events, never as outcomes.
Exclusions were not edited. Hashes were computed after the last edit, and exclusions/2023-11-07.json was confirmed unchanged against git HEAD.
